node.statement: In the characteristic-value notation used by the Leray-Schauder formula, nu is a characteristic value of A exactly when ker(I-nu A) is nonzero. For nu in (0,1), this is equivalent to A having the real eigenvalue lambda=nu^{-1}>1; conversely every real eigenvalue lambda>1 gives nu=lambda^{-1} in (0,1). The reciprocal change of variable preserves algebraic multiplicity. Hence beta is precisely the total algebraic multiplicity m_> of the real eigenvalues lambda>1 of A.
